title: Vulnerabilities in VPNs: Paper presented at the Privacy Enhancing Technologies Symposium 2024
excerpt: The “port shadow” exploit in connection‑tracking frameworks is outlined, showing how attackers can hijack VPN traffic and deanonymize users, along with mitigation advice for providers and users.

title: New VPN Port Shadow Vulnerabilities Expose Encrypted Traffic to Attackers
excerpt: Details of four attacks enabled by the newly identified port‑shadow vulnerability across OpenVPN, OpenConnect, and WireGuard are presented, demonstrating how encrypted traffic can be intercepted and users de‑anonymized.

title: Unpacking the "Port Shadow" VPN Vulnerability
excerpt: The mechanics of port‑shadow attacks are explained, along with configurations that can prevent traffic hijacking, DNS redirection, and port scanning.

title: How Geoblocking Limits Digital Access in Sanctioned States
excerpt: An examination of how online platforms, wary of sanctions compliance, voluntarily block users in embargoed countries, shrinking the open internet for millions in places like Iran, Syria, and Russia.

title: The web really isn’t worldwide – every country has different access
excerpt: An exploration of how websites and services curate access by country, combining government censorship with corporate geoblocking to create vastly different online experiences for global users.

title: The same app can pose a bigger security and privacy threat depending on the country where you download it, study finds
excerpt: Findings reveal that Android versions of the same apps differ by region, with higher tracker counts and more dangerous permissions in some countries, raising privacy and security concerns.

title: Shining a light in the dark: Measuring global internet shutdowns
excerpt: A BigQuery‑powered pipeline is described, surfacing verified data on internet shutdowns in 35 countries across 2022.

title: Cloud and consequences: Internet censorship data enters the transformation age
excerpt: Collaboration efforts to process 80 TB of global censorship measurements are detailed, turning raw data into actionable insights for researchers and activists.

title: Making Censorship Data More User Friendly
excerpt: An open‑source pipeline is outlined, designed to clean, enrich, and fingerprint censorship measurements, producing ready‑to‑use dashboards for policymakers and journalists.

title: Profiling Internet Censors: Methods to Measure and Locate Censorship Devices
excerpt: Techniques for fingerprinting middleboxes, mapping their autonomous‑system locations, and tracking evolving censorship infrastructure worldwide are presented.

title: An analysis of a large-scale HTTPS interception
excerpt: Kazakhstan’s nationwide HTTPS interception campaigns are dissected, detailing certificate deployment tactics and recommending mitigations against future man‑in‑the‑middle attacks.
